params.description: URLs referencing publicly available Federal Enterprise Architecture (FEA) documentation from OMB (published 2007) and references to the NIST govdocs test corpus were identified in Office documents on RM#2. These are public government reference materials that IT professionals and analysts routinely access and embed in their work. This does not indicate that sensitive data was being stolen, but rather documents normal reference material usage.

Email addresses from government personnel (Eric_P._Lauer@omb.eop.gov, mmun@loc.gov) were recovered from browser cookies and embedded hyperlinks within Office documents on RM#2. These are artifacts of web browsing and document metadata, not evidence of communication using the device for data theft. Email addresses embedded in cookies and documents are normal browsing residue for users who interact with government websites and communications.

Browser cookie artifacts reference email addresses informant@questionmarket.com and informant@serving-sys, suggesting the user had web service accounts or registrations. While these domains exist, the presence of cookies does not establish that these accounts were used for coordinated data theft. No actual email traffic or data exfiltration to these addresses is documented in the evidence.

The CD-R contains three standard Windows sample image files (Koala.jpg, Penguins.jpg, Tulips.jpg) with 2009 modification dates - these are pre-installed Windows sample images included in all Windows installations, not intentional decoys. More significantly, the CD contains two large compressed archive files: winter_whether_advisory.zip (16.4 MB, modified 2014-12-16) and my_favorite_movies.7z (100 KB, modified 2015-01-08), which were stored in deleted directory sessions alongside the categorized business project folders.
